summary.text: 飞 is the simplified form of 飛. The traditional graph is a whole-graph picture interpreted as a bird in flight; 飞 commonly means “to fly.”

formation.text: The traditional graph 飛 is pictographic: its whole form is interpreted as a bird in flight with outspread wings. The curated seal-script-style image illustrates this interpretation, but is a modern redraw rather than an ancient artifact.

components.text: The whole historical graph is interpreted as a bird in flight. It is not an internal component of modern 飞.

history.text: The curated seal-script-style redraw shows 飛 with a central upright and spreading sides, illustrating the traditional bird-in-flight interpretation. It does not establish the exact form of a particular ancient inscription.

A study reports no oracle-bone form of 飛 and cites an Eastern Zhou form in the Qin Gong gui. Chu manuscript, seal-script, and 說文 forms are also displayed, but they do not establish a continuous dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 飞 as the simplified form of 飛; it does not explain when or how the reduced shape first arose.

uncertainties.text: The exact appearance and earliest attestation of 飛, a continuous chronology of its forms, and the earlier history of 飞’s reduced shape remain unresolved.

senses.text: 飛 is glossed as a bird in flight, and early literary examples use it for flying. The composition dates of those works and the earliest secure surviving written attestation are unresolved.
Rapid movement is recorded as a sense, but its chronology and whether it developed from “fly” are unresolved.
“High” or “elevated” is recorded as a sense; its chronology and relation to “fly” are unresolved.

limitations.text: Rapid movement, high, unexpected, and unfounded are recorded senses, but their chronology and semantic paths from “fly” are not established; they are not connected here as developments.

The evidence reports uses of 飛 for 非 and graphic or borrowing relations involving 蜚, but does not establish their earliest attestations, chronology, or sound comparisons. No borrowing mechanism is asserted here.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw representing an ancient script form
items.caption: This modern redraw presents 飛 in a Shuowen seal-script style. Its central upright stroke and spreading side forms illustrate the traditional interpretation of the graph as a bird with extended wings in flight.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style 飛 glyph with a tall central stroke and spreading side forms, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: The candidate is identified as a Shuowen seal-script-style redraw, and the cited graphic-history source describes 飛 as resembling outstretched wings in flight. It gives a useful visual example of that interpretation while making clear that it is a modern reconstruction.
